author: FX.Sniffer
text:
Starting with previous posts, showing the complete trades from opening to close in addition to overview analysis.

My main trading time frames are H4 & H1. I might use the minimum
indicators for confluence sake, such as Trend Lines, Channels and
sometimes Oscillators for divergence signals.

The core of my trading technique is tracing the order flow and trading Price Action at decision areas.

Based on this equation Volatility = High Volume + Low Liquidity, I will be using some terms that might have the same meaning as follows:

Base = Cluster = Equilibrium = Indecision = Balance = Stable = Normal = Efficient = Range = Consolidation = Flag

Decision = Imbalance = Unstable = Abnormal = Inefficient = Momentum = Impulse = Liquidity Gap/Spike = Engulf = Pole

Corrective Moves = Rebalancing

Level = Zone = Area

Decision Point = Supply / Demand

Pivot Zone = S/R Flip/Swap = Key Level

Broken = Ignored

False Breakout = Fakeout = Stop Run = Stop Hunt = Trap

Positioning / Accumulation = Liquidation / Distribution

You can find my following articles in the
 Markepedia
, and I recommend reading all of the other great articles in there:

1).
 Order Flow

2).
 Trend Direction / Highs & Lows

3).
 Key Levels and Price Action There

4).
 Stacked Orders/Zones

5).
 Momentum Away / Liquidity Gap

6).
 Fakeouts

All comments and critics are most welcomed.

Welcome to my journal!

Edit: I was one of the co-founders of RTM
 and it was fun for quite sometime but good things never last. I've
decided to seperate myself from RTM and now I have my own place where I
call home. This journal will remain here for the old time's sake.

text:
This short trade follows the previous long.

had a DD but this time I didn't set a SL, so
 I waited for price at higher supply zone. However, my 2nd entry as it
shown in last chart wasn't a right decision.

Explaining the trapped traders...

On the right side of attached gold chart
there is a marked demand zone, this zone was a very clear and strong
demand twice. One time to leave the zone at ( A ), another one as retest
 as a spike at ( B ). What do you think traders did when it came back at
 ( C )? They bought it. Well it happens that it was not the good thing
to do here so they got trapped at ( C ). When price came back near their
 order price at ( D ) they could get out of their longs hence
mechanically becoming sellers.

Done..closed them all...

Another example of trapped traders and price behavior there...

To evaluate myself I think I've been doing good with swings, but I have three weaknesses:

1) I need to take into consideration the LTF levels and do more trading on LTF.

2) I need to work on my entry to avoid as much as possible any drawdown.

3) I need to be more flexible with my TP as I'm with my SL.
